title: Autopsy and Verdict
premise: Insurance investigator Juniper Dunmore is hired to verify a life-insurance claim tied to the exhumation of town founder Edmund Hale — and discovers the coffin empty. Juniper's photographic memory of a decades-old newspaper photo reveals the buried man was never Hale but a lookalike, meaning someone faked the founder's death and the real Edmund may still be alive, draining his own estate through a shell company. As Juniper closes in, he uncovers that Hale's loyal housekeeper, Mabel, helped stage the swap out of love, and that the 'heir' pressing the claim is Hale himself in a new identity, dying and desperate to come home. In the end, Juniper must choose between the truth that will ruin the town's founding myth and the mercy of letting a dying man be buried under his own name — he chooses a verdict that closes the case and honors both loyalty and truth.
about_author: Felix Marchetti is a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent eleven years investigating suspicious deaths before turning to fiction. He writes in a converted boathouse, where he insists every plot twist must survive the same scrutiny he once gave a forged signature.

chapters.title: The Empty Mahogany
chapters.summary: Juniper Dunmore, POV. Called to verify a claim on the Hale estate, Juniper witnesses the exhumation of town founder Edmund Hale — and finds the coffin empty except for river stones. His photographic memory snags on a detail from the original 1978 burial photo: the hands of the corpse were wrong. Emotional beat: professional confidence cracking into unease as the town's sacred history tilts.

chapters.title: What Mabel Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. He interviews Mabel Voss, Hale's aging housekeeper and sole beneficiary-adjacent witness, whose answers are too polished — until a slip about 'the second suit' confirms a body swap. Meanwhile someone ransacks Juniper's office, hunting his case file. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by the realization that a kind woman may be the architect.

chapters.title: The Man in the Mirror Claim
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Tracing the shell company draining the estate, he confronts 'Gideon Marsh,' the claimant — and recognizes Hale's eyes in a younger face, surgically altered, terminally ill. Marsh confesses: he faked his death to watch the town love him freely, and Mabel helped out of devotion. Emotional beat: climax — Juniper's certainty collapses into compassion as the truth demands a verdict.

chapters.title: Buried Under His Own Name
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Hale dies within days; Mabel begs Juniper to let him lie in the empty grave as himself. Juniper files a verdict of misadventure, seals the swap in his memory alone, and the town reburies its founder — truly, this time — with Mabel beside the coffin. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution; loyalty and truth reconciled in a lie Juniper can live with.
